blocks.heading: What this section covers
blocks.text: Set out the main measures of monetary policy, trace how each works through the banking system, and weigh their strength and drawbacks.

blocks.heading: The two main measures
blocks.text: The first measure is changing interest rates: the central bank raises or lowers the rate at which it lends to commercial banks, which tend to move their loan and deposit rates the same way. The second measure is controlling the growth of the money supply: the central bank can sell government securities to banks, which pay from their reserves and then hold less to lend, or tighten the rules under which banks create new deposits through lending.

blocks.heading: A rate rise traced
blocks.text: Suppose the policy rate rises from 4% to 8%. Etosha Gate Lodge plans a N$150 000 kitchen extension on a bank loan: at 4% the yearly interest is 0.04 x N$150 000 = N$6 000, at 8% it is 0.08 x N$150 000 = N$12 000, so the lodge is likely to postpone. Households move the same way - dearer credit, better-rewarded saving - so borrowing falls, fewer new deposits are created, and the growth of the money supply slows.

blocks.heading: Monetary measures or supply-side measures?
blocks.text: The boundary: a monetary measure works on the cost of borrowing and the stock of money; a supply-side measure works on the economy's capacity to produce. The test is to ask what the measure changes - the price of money, or what the economy can produce. A grant helping Kaoko Juice buy bottling equipment is supply-side; a policy-rate rise is monetary.

blocks.heading: Strength and drawbacks
blocks.text: Strength: interest-rate changes work through the whole banking system at once, reaching households and firms across the economy within days. Drawbacks: the effects arrive with a delay, spending financed without bank credit responds less, and dearer borrowing may hold back firms' building projects and jobs. A rate rise cools credit-financed spending faster than it cools a cash-only market stall, in Vietnam as in Namibia.

blocks.heading: Connections
blocks.text: The interest-rate mechanism runs through the household decisions of topic 3.2 and the borrowing costs of firms in topic 3.7; the aims it serves belong with the role of government in topic 4.1.
